domain: scientific prediction from large measured or simulated data sets
why_it_matters: it can learn useful patterns when hand-written rules are incomplete, but the result still needs tests outside the examples used for fitting
keeps: many adjustable weights that turn inputs into predictions

everyday_anchor: A lab notebook may contain many examples of inputs and outcomes. Deep learning is the adjustable recipe that tries to match those examples, then must be checked on a new page of the notebook.

title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks

domain: fast prediction for families of scientific simulations

title: Graphs And Geometric Learning
common_problem: many scientific objects are not simple rows of numbers; their connections matter
domain: systems made of interacting parts, meshes, molecules, or spatial relations
why_it_matters: it lets the model respect the structure of the object instead of flattening away important relations
keeps: nodes, edges, spatial relations, and symmetry rules that should not change the answer
leaves_out: interactions or long-range effects not represented in the graph
failure_boundary: the graph can encode the wrong neighborhood, hide missing interactions, or fail when the mesh changes
everyday_anchor: A molecule, mesh, or network is not just a list. The connections decide what can influence what.

domain: changing systems where time evolution is part of the model

keeps: a learned rate rule inside a time-stepping calculation

failure_boundary: small learned-rate errors can accumulate until long-time predictions drift away from the real system

title: Symbolic Regression And Model Discovery

domain: turning data into equations people can inspect
why_it_matters: a short equation can be tested, criticized, and reused more easily than a large fitted model
keeps: candidate formulas that can be written, checked, and compared
leaves_out: terms that were not searched, variables that were not measured, and physics not excited by the data
failure_boundary: a neat formula can fit the training data while using the wrong variables or failing on a changed experiment
everyday_anchor: Start with the observed object, name what must be predicted, then test the claim on a changed case.
